description: Login server: passkey sign-in, token grants, refresh chains, rate limits, kicks, sweepers. Hand-authored; see observability/ and the observability skill.

panels.title: Accounts
panels.description: Rows in the account table, read at most every 30 s.

panels.title: Live login sessions
panels.description: Browser logins that have not expired yet.

panels.title: Usable refresh tokens
panels.description: Refresh tokens that could still be spent: roughly one per signed-in device.

panels.title: Open ceremonies
panels.description: Passkey ceremonies started and neither finished nor expired.

panels.title: Refresh token reuse (1 h)
panels.description: A spent refresh token was presented again, so a copy of it exists elsewhere and its chain was revoked. Anything above zero deserves a look.

panels.title: Assertions by result
panels.description: WebAuthn assertion verification at the login page. unknown_credential is a passkey this server has no row for; failed covers a bad challenge, a bad signature and a stale ceremony.

panels.title: Assertion verification latency
panels.description: Time inside RelyingParty.finishAssertion only; the database round trips around it are not included.

panels.title: Ceremony calls by step and result
panels.description: Every browser-facing call of the WebAuthn controller. session_refused is a login session that was expired, bound to another browser or banned.

panels.title: Registrations and recoveries
panels.description: Credentials stored by kind, and recovery-code redemptions. A rise in recovery rejected is someone guessing codes.

panels.title: Grants by client, flow and result
panels.description: start opens a login, exchange redeems the authorization code, refresh resumes from a stored token.

panels.title: Refused grants by reason
panels.description: The finer reason behind INVALID_REQUEST / INVALID_GRANT / ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE, which the client is never told. banned is an account that may not log in.

panels.title: Refused grants by client and flow
Browser-side session refusals by reason
panels.description: Refusals at the login page and at /session/complete: another browser, an expired or already used session, a ban.

panels.title: Invalid api tokens
panels.description: Api tokens the admin API turned away with a 401: expired, forged or of the wrong kind.

panels.title: Refresh rotations
panels.description: Reuse of a spent token is counted under the revocations panel, not as a reason here.

panels.title: Refresh chain revocations
panels.description: reuse is the theft signal. sign_out is a client leaving; account_terminated counts accounts that were banned, kicked or recovered.

panels.title: Authorization codes
panels.description: issued at the end of a browser login, consumed by the client's exchange. refused is a code that was unknown, expired or already spent.

panels.title: Account state held
panels.description: Row counts, each re-read at most every 30 s.

panels.title: Denials by bucket
panels.description: 429s from the per-address limiter. The bucket is the endpoint; the address is never recorded.

panels.title: Live limiter windows
panels.description: Windows held in memory; the 10-minute sweep drops the ones idle for 30 minutes. Growth without bound means the sweep is not running.

panels.title: Kick orders published
panels.description: One per ended set of sessions (ban, GM kick, recovery). error means Valkey could not take it and the player keeps playing until they disconnect.

panels.title: Kick publish latency
panels.description: Paid inside the GM or recovery request. The command timeout is 2 s, so a flat line near it is Valkey being down.

panels.title: Bus appends
panels.description: The stream appender's own tally, read from the bus module.

panels.title: GM actions
panels.description: refused is a GM without the authority, or a target they do not outrank.

panels.title: Sweep runs and failures
panels.description: The five jobs share one scheduler thread, so a stalled run delays the others.

title: Login Server
